subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 50 g but only 40 g is obtained. What is the percentage yield?
questions.explain: percentage yield = (40/50)×100 = 80%.

questions.q: What charge does an oxide ion have?
questions.explain: Oxygen gains two electrons to form an O2- ion.

questions.q: Why is the relative mass of an electron taken as very small?
options: An electron's mass is negligible compared with a proton or neutron
questions.explain: An electron's mass is about 1/1836 of a proton's, so it is treated as negligible.

questions.q: How many moles are in 100 g of calcium carbonate, CaCO3? (Mr = 100)
questions.explain: moles = mass/Mr = 100/100 = 1 mol.

questions.q: A compound contains 0.2 mol carbon and 0.4 mol hydrogen. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explain: The ratio 0.2:0.4 simplifies to 1:2, giving CH2.

questions.q: What is the mass of 0.5 mol of CaCO3? (Mr = 100)
questions.explain: mass = moles × Mr = 0.5 × 100 = 50 g.

questions.q: How many moles are in 80 g of NaOH? (Mr = 40)
questions.explain: moles = mass/Mr = 80/40 = 2 mol.

questions.q: Why is a high atom economy desirable in industry?
options: It produces less waste and uses resources efficiently
questions.explain: High atom economy means more reactant atoms end up in the useful product, reducing waste.

questions.q: What is the formula of the ionic compound aluminium oxide, from Al³⁺ and O²⁻?
questions.explain: Balancing charges (2×Al³⁺ = +6, 3×O²⁻ = −6) gives Al2O3.

questions.q: Which of these is a compound?
options: A mixture of salt and sand
questions.explain: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen chemically bonded together.

questions.q: The change of state directly from solid to gas is called:
questions.explain: Sublimation is the change directly from solid to gas without becoming a liquid.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a neutron?
questions.explain: Neutrons are electrically neutral, with a relative charge of 0.

questions.q: Which scientist proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy shells?
questions.explain: Bohr suggested electrons occupy fixed shells (energy levels) around the nucleus.

questions.q: What is the formula of the compound formed from Mg²⁺ and Cl⁻ ions?
questions.explain: Two Cl⁻ ions balance one Mg²⁺ ion, giving MgCl2.

questions.q: Isotopes of the same element have the same number of protons but different numbers of:
questions.explain: Isotopes differ only in their number of neutrons.

questions.q: Graphene is best described as:
options: A simple molecule of two carbons
A single layer of carbon atoms arranged in hexagons
questions.explain: Graphene is a single layer of graphite, one atom thick, in a hexagonal arrangement.

questions.q: A compound contains 0.3 mol of nitrogen and 0.9 mol of hydrogen. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explain: The ratio 0.3:0.9 simplifies to 1:3, giving NH3.

questions.q: What did the alpha-particle scattering experiment suggest about the nucleus?
options: It is large and spread out
It is small, dense and positively charged
questions.explain: Most alpha particles passed through, but a few were deflected, showing a small dense positive nucleus.

questions.q: Which subatomic particle is found outside the nucleus?
questions.explain: Electrons occupy shells (energy levels) outside the nucleus.

questions.q: In the particle model, what is true of particles in a gas?
options: Touching but able to move past each other
Far apart and moving quickly in all directions
questions.explain: Gas particles are far apart and move randomly at high speed.

questions.q: In which state are particles most closely packed and only able to vibrate in fixed positions?
questions.explain: In a solid, particles are tightly packed in a regular arrangement and only vibrate.

questions.q: Which of these substances has the lowest boiling point?
questions.explain: Simple molecular substances like oxygen have only weak intermolecular forces, so very low boiling points.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Chemistry (1CH0) specification; Key Concepts In Chemistry
